newsitem.title: KENYA: African leaders meet in Nairobi on Zaire crisis.
newsitem.headline: African leaders meet in Nairobi on Zaire crisis.

text.p: African leaders opened talks in the Kenyan capital Nairobi on Tuesday on the war in eastern Zaire where more than a million Hutu refugees are at risk.
"The conflict in eastern Zaire poses a serious threat to the stability of the entire region," host Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi told fellow leaders at the start of talks at State House.

But Zaire boycotted the summit, saying it could not attend any talks until Rwandan troops withdrew from its territory. A Zairean flag was on the conference table in front of an empty seat for Kinshasa's representative.
Moi met the leaders of Tanzania, Ethiopia, Uganda, Rwanda, Zambia and Eritrea for talks on Africa's most serious crisis since the 1994 genocide of Tutsis in Rwanda in the same "Great Lakes" region.
Cameroon was represented by its foreign minister. The secretary-general of the Organisation of African Unity was also at the summit with Burundi mediator Julius Nyerere, a former Tanzanian president.
